label: Fires at GO late in episode after rewarded a2-to-S2, growing with trial number.
short_terms: (phase == GO) * np.maximum(ep_trial - 82, 0) * last_is("a2 S2 r") ;; (phase == GO) * (ep_trial >= 82) * last_is("a2 S2 r") ;; (phase == GO) * np.maximum(ep_trial - 82, 0)
terms: (phase == GO) * np.maximum(ep_trial - 82, 0) * last_is("a2 S2 r") ;; (phase == GO) * (ep_trial >= 82) * last_is("a2 S2 r") ;; (phase == GO) * np.maximum(ep_trial - 82, 0) ;; (phase == GO) * np.maximum(ep_trial - 82, 0) * (prev_action == 2) * (prev_reward == 1) ;; (phase == GO) * np.maximum(ep_trial - 82, 0) * (belief_lo < 0) ;; (phase == GO) * np.maximum(ep_trial - 82, 0) * last_is("a2 S2 r") * np.clip(-belief_lo, 0, 6) ;; (phase == GO) * (ep_trial >= 82) * last_is("a2 S2 r") * (tv("reward", -2) == 1)
explanation: Only active at GO in the last ~18 trials of the episode. Magnitude is driven by the previous trial being a2 -> S2 rewarded (common rewarded a2); in that case it ramps up with ep_trial past ~82 (to ~2 by trial 96-99), otherwise it stays near zero. The timing baseline alone over-predicts after all other histories; the short form gates the late ramp on last_is(a2 S2 r) and subtracts the generic ramp. D1 and D2 are always zero. The free fit adds a small belief (S2-good log-odds) and reward-two-trials-back refinement (+0.03 dev R^2). Observed-only; no future variables.

terms: (phase == GO) * np.maximum(ep_trial - 82, 0) * last_is("a2 S2 r") * np.clip(-belief_lo, 0, 6)

issues: The claims hold up. Test R^2 beyond timing: the recorded short form scores 0.684. The ramp x last_is(a2 S2 r) term alone scores 0.508, and the step x last_is(a2 S2 r) alone scores 0.342. Swapping the condition for prev_reward + prev_state scores 0.441, and adding last_is(a2 S1 r) adds nothing (0.683). So the a2->S2 rewarded condition and the late ramp are both real. D1 and D2 are exactly zero, as claimed.

The second term, (phase==GO)*(ep_trial>=82)*last_is(a2 S2 r), gets weight -0.064 and is only a fitted offset. Dropping it gives 0.682 test, so a two-term form (gated ramp plus a negative generic ramp) says the same thing more simply.

The 'grows with trial number' claim is partly about how often the feature fires, not how strongly. In the misses output, whenever the feature is on it sits near 1.7-2.05, already at t93-94. The ramp mostly captures that firing becomes more likely as the episode goes on. Step functions at 82/88/90/94 do worse than the ramp (0.42-0.50), so the ramp is still the better description of expected activation.

Misses shows no large systematic error class. The biggest is GO after '?' (window start, previous trial not observable) at +0.034, where the feature fires at full strength but cannot be predicted from inside the window. Every other previous-trial cell is over-predicted by at most about 0.016. There are occasional false positives at t99 after a2 S2 rewarded when the two trials before were unrewarded, which hints at a weak dependence on longer reward history. But tv('reward',-2) adds nothing (0.683), and belief_lo<-1 adds only +0.013 (0.697).
No future variables are used. Everything here is observed-only.
